standard.title: Interpret, translate and convey meaning
standard.description: apply strategies to interpret, translate and convey meaning in familiar and some unfamiliar non-verbal, spoken and written cultural contexts
standard.prior_knowledge: Students entering at Y7-8 have experience of moving between the target language and English in home and community contexts. They can interpret informally and may conduct transactions or conversations across languages. They have not yet applied systematic translation strategies, managed formal register conversion, or produced structured bilingual texts in academic contexts.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students apply strategies to interpret, translate and convey meaning in familiar and some unfamiliar cultural contexts — including register conversion, cultural concept challenges, interpreting for others, and producing bilingual texts.

nodes.label: Register conversion and cultural connotation
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can convert language between formal and informal registers and identify cultural connotations of words that affect translation meaning.
nodes.minimum_width: Convert at least one informal spoken expression into formal written register, and identify at least two words or expressions where cultural connotation affects meaning in translation.
nodes.typical_width: Use formal register for speeches and formal contexts; convert informal spoken language into appropriate register; discuss cultural connotations of words expressing emotion or social relationship; identify expressions whose meaning depends on cultural context rather than lexical equivalence.
wider: Compare how the same concept is expressed with different connotations in target language and English — explain what the difference reveals about cultural values
Analyse a formal text and an informal version of the same content — identify every register marker that distinguishes them and explain the cultural logic behind each
nodes.hinge_reason: Register conversion and cultural connotation awareness are prerequisites for all translation and interpretation work. Students who cannot manage these will consistently produce culturally inappropriate or misleading translations.

response_modes.reason: Register conversion requires analytical attention to what makes formal language formal — not only substituting vocabulary but understanding the underlying cultural logic. Explicit analysis of register markers builds this systematic awareness.

success_criteria: Converts at least one informal expression into formal register appropriately
Identifies at least two words where cultural connotation affects translation meaning

nodes.label: Interpreting for others and managing untranslatables
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can act as interpreter for target language and English speakers, applying clarifying and rephrasing strategies, and handle idioms and culturally-embedded language that cannot be translated directly.
nodes.minimum_width: Interpret at least one exchange between target language and English speakers using at least one clarifying or rephrasing strategy, and handle at least one idiom or untranslatable expression with an appropriate strategy.
nodes.typical_width: Act as interpreter for visitors — clarifying, rephrasing and explaining cultural concepts; apply strategies to translate idioms, fables and culturally-embedded stories; read bilingual texts and identify expressions that cannot be directly translated; use dictionaries and digital tools to support translation.
wider: Interpret in a scenario involving a cultural concept that has no English equivalent — explain the concept to both parties and discuss the cultural background required to understand it

Compare own informal interpreting experience from home and community with the structured interpreting strategies introduced in this descriptor — identify what is already intuitive and what requires explicit development

response_modes.reason: Interpreting and untranslatable expression handling must be practised across varied cultural contexts — different audiences, different types of culturally-embedded language. Varied interpreting scenarios build flexible, audience-aware mediation capacity.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Many background language learner entry students already interpret informally in family and community contexts. Width investment here formalises this experience — building the conscious strategies that transform intuitive bilingual mediation into skilled interpreting practice.
success_criteria: Interprets an exchange using at least one clarifying or rephrasing strategy
Handles at least one idiom or untranslatable expression with an appropriate strategy and explanation

nodes.label: Producing bilingual texts
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can produce bilingual texts — subtitles, translated resources, cross-language explanations — that accurately convey meaning across both languages for a specific purpose.
nodes.minimum_width: Produce at least one bilingual text with accurate meaning transfer, demonstrating at least one deliberate translation decision beyond word-for-word substitution.
nodes.typical_width: Produce bilingual texts — subtitles, translated materials, cross-curricular explanations for target language peers; apply translation strategies; rewrite lyrics or story lines in the target language; use resources to create Chinese translations of English texts.
wider: Produce a bilingual text for a real audience — evaluate accuracy and cultural appropriateness with a target audience member and revise
Reflect on the translation decisions made — identify which were straightforward, which required cultural judgment, and what the process revealed about the two languages

response_modes.reason: Bilingual text production integrates register conversion (node 1) and interpreting strategies (node 2) into a full translation act. The teaching investment is in creating real or realistic audience conditions where translation decisions carry genuine communicative weight.

success_criteria: Produces a bilingual text with accurate meaning transfer in both languages
Demonstrates at least one deliberate translation decision beyond word-for-word substitution
